description:
## Why

Modern TLS, code signing, and sigstore heavily use ECDSA P-384. Currently rejected by `pkix-path`.

OID: `1.2.840.10045.4.3.3` (ecdsa-with-SHA384). Algorithm parameters MUST be absent per RFC 5758 §3.2.

## What

1. New unit struct `EcdsaP384Verifier` behind `feature = "p384"` in `pkix-path/src/lib.rs`. Mirror `EcdsaP256Verifier` at `lib.rs:1867`.
2. Add `p384 = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["ecdsa", "pkcs8"] }` to `workspace.dependencies` and pkix-path's optional deps.
3. OID dispatch in `DefaultVerifier` (`lib.rs:3047`) for `1.2.840.10045.4.3.3`.
4. Update `rustcrypto` umbrella feature to include p384.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `EcdsaP384Verifier` impls `SignatureVerifier` and verifies a known-good signature from independent test vectors (NIST CAVS or RustCrypto p384 crate fixtures).
- [ ] Tampered-signature test rejects cleanly.
- [ ] At least one real-world P-384 chain added to `pkix-difftest/tests/fixtures/` and confirmed validating (suggest: a sigstore/Fulcio cert, which uses P-384).
- [ ] `DefaultVerifier` dispatches to it.
- [ ] No `unsafe`. `pkix-path` stays `no_std` (p384 default-features=false is no_std-capable).

## Filed as

PKIX-gphz child #2. Modern TLS and sigstore.
title: crypto: ECDSA P-384 + SHA-384 SignatureVerifier
